guideTitle: The Best Docking Stations with 2.5Gb Ethernet, and Which Ones Confirm It
metaDescription: Only some docks sold as 2.5GbE list it clearly. We compared seven on confirmed Ethernet speed, displays, charging and ports, and flag the ones to check.
introParagraphs: A 2.5Gb Ethernet port only helps if your network supports it: a 2.5GbE router or switch, or a fast NAS. On a standard Gigabit network, a 2.5GbE dock runs at Gigabit speed.

Of the seven docks here, only two listings clearly state 2.5GbE: the UGREEN Revodok Max 213 (Thunderbolt 4) and the TobenONE 16-in-1 (USB-C). The others don't confirm the speed in their summaries, and the Plugable is described elsewhere as Gigabit, so check before buying.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

ugreen-13-in-1-thunderbolt-4-revodok-max.summary: A 13-in-1 Thunderbolt 4 dock with 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet, dual 4K@60Hz or 8K, 90W and an SD 4.0 reader.
ugreen-13-in-1-thunderbolt-4-revodok-max.description:
The UGREEN Revodok Max 213 combines Thunderbolt 4 with 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet, the feature this guide is about, plus dual 4K at 60Hz or a single 8K display, 90W charging and a UHS-II-class SD/TF 4.0 reader.

It was the most expensive dock here at the time of writing, and 90W is below the 100W some laptops use.
ugreen-13-in-1-thunderbolt-4-revodok-max.skipIf: Your laptop has plain USB-C; the TobenONE 16-in-1 lists 2.5GbE over USB-C.

plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.summary: A Thunderbolt 4 certified dock with 100W charging, dual 4K or single 6K output, SD and Ethernet.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is a certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with 100W charging, dual 4K or single 6K output, six USB ports, SD and Ethernet, driverless on Mac and Windows.

In other listings its Ethernet port is described as Gigabit, not 2.5GbE; confirm the speed before buying it for a 2.5GbE network.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.bestFor: Thunderbolt and recent MacBook users who want dependable dual-display docking.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.skipIf: 2.5GbE is essential; the UGREEN Revodok Max 213 confirms it.

tobenone-16-in-1-triple-4k.summary: A 16-in-1 dock with 2.5Gbps Ethernet, three 4K HDMI outputs, 7 USB ports and a 150W power supply.
tobenone-16-in-1-triple-4k.description:
The TobenONE 16-in-1 confirms 2.5Gbps Ethernet on a USB-C dock and adds three HDMI outputs for triple 4K, seven USB ports and a 150W power supply.

The listing summary doesn't state how the three displays are driven or their refresh rate; on Macs and some laptops, three displays may require DisplayLink or not be possible.
tobenone-16-in-1-triple-4k.bestFor: USB-C laptops on a 2.5GbE network with several monitors.
tobenone-16-in-1-triple-4k.skipIf: You use a Mac; the TobenONE 18-in-2 targets MacBooks.

anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.summary: A 14-port DisplayLink dock with triple 4K at 60Hz, 140W output and a cooling fan.
anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.description:
The Anker Prime DL7400 drives three 4K displays at 60Hz through DisplayLink, which is uncommon, with 140W total output, a built-in cooling fan and a display status indicator.

Anker lists it for Windows laptops with the latest DisplayLink driver installed. It isn't Thunderbolt certified.
cons: Ethernet speed not stated in summary
anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.skipIf: 2.5GbE is essential; confirm the Ethernet speed first, or choose the UGREEN or TobenONE 16-in-1.

tobenone-18-in-1-triple-4k.summary: An 18-in-1 dock with triple 4K via HDMI/DP/USB-C, 8 USB ports up to 10Gbps and a 150W adapter.
tobenone-18-in-1-triple-4k.description:
The TobenONE 18-in-1 offers the most ports here: eight USB ports up to 10Gbps, triple 4K output across HDMI, DisplayPort and USB-C, and a 150W adapter with a 20W fast-charge port. It lists Windows and ChromeOS compatibility.

The listing summary doesn't confirm 2.5GbE, so check the Ethernet speed.
tobenone-18-in-1-triple-4k.bestFor: Windows or Chromebook desks needing many ports.
tobenone-18-in-1-triple-4k.skipIf: 2.5GbE is essential; the TobenONE 16-in-1 confirms it.

tobenone-18-in-2-macbook.summary: A MacBook-focused 18-in-2 dock with dual 4K@60Hz and a 150W adapter.
tobenone-18-in-2-macbook.description:
The TobenONE 18-in-2 is aimed at MacBooks, connecting over two cables to support dual 4K at 60Hz, with many USB and data ports and a 150W adapter.

The listing summary doesn't confirm 2.5GbE or give exact port details.
cons: Uses two ports on the Mac

baseus-spacemate-11-in-1.badge: Compact Triple-Display Dock (Ethernet Speed to Confirm)
baseus-spacemate-11-in-1.summary: An 11-in-1 Baseus dock with triple display, 10Gbps USB, Ethernet and 100W PD.
baseus-spacemate-11-in-1.description:
The Baseus Spacemate is a compact 11-in-1 dock with triple display output over 4K HDMI and DisplayPort, 10Gbps USB-C and USB-A, Ethernet, audio and 100W charging, with a power adapter included.

The listing summary doesn't confirm 2.5GbE.
baseus-spacemate-11-in-1.skipIf: 2.5GbE is essential; the UGREEN or TobenONE 16-in-1 confirms it.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Only the UGREEN 213 and TobenONE 16-in-1 state it here.
You need 2.5GbE on the router, switch or NAS to benefit.
Thunderbolt docks need a Thunderbolt/USB4 port for full bandwidth.
Displays and wattage vary; triple display depends on your laptop.

faq.a: Only if your network supports it and you move large files, for example to a NAS.

faq.q: Will it work on a Gigabit network?

faq.a: The UGREEN Revodok Max 213 and TobenONE 16-in-1.
No. The TobenONE 16-in-1 offers 2.5GbE over USB-C.
Yes, but wired Ethernet is typically more consistent for large transfers.

bottomLine: If 2.5GbE is the priority, choose a dock that states it: the UGREEN Revodok Max 213 for Thunderbolt laptops, or the TobenONE 16-in-1 over USB-C for less.
The other docks here may suit your displays and ports, but confirm their Ethernet speed before buying for a 2.5GbE network.
